analysis.investment_thesis: Jyothy Labs is a financially sound consumer staples business with a decade of earnings, but at P/E 23.9x and P/B 6.09x it trades at roughly 2.1x its Graham Number (~INR 112), offering no margin of safety whatsoever. The intelligent investor does not pay premium prices for branded goods; he waits for Mr. Market to offer them at a discount.
key_strengths: Virtually debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.04, borrowings only INR 61 Cr vs equity INR 2,050 Cr)
10 consecutive years of positive earnings with net profit CAGR of 19.6% — meets the multi-year track record requirement
Interest coverage of ~89x (EBITDA INR 536 Cr / finance cost INR 6 Cr) and 5/5 years of positive OCF
key_risks: Valuation is dangerously stretched: P/B 6.09x is 4x my maximum threshold of 1.5x; paying INR 238 against a Graham Number of ~INR 112
Revenue growth is modest — 9-year CAGR of only 6.7% — yet the market prices this as a high-growth compounder
OCF declined sharply to INR 311 Cr in 2025 from INR 458 Cr in 2024 despite record net profit, a worrying divergence
red_flags: P/B of 6.09x implies investors are paying INR 6 for every INR 1 of tangible book — pure speculation on brand intangibles
Graham Number (~INR 112) is 53% below the current price of INR 238; no margin of safety exists at any reasonable downside scenario
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Jyothy Labs passes my qualitative screen admirably — it is a real business with recognizable brands (Ujala, Pril, Exo, Maxo), a long operating history since 1983, a clean balance sheet, and genuine earnings power. Finance costs have collapsed from INR 62 Cr in 2016 to just INR 6 Cr in 2025, a remarkable deleveraging story. The business earns a ROCE of 24.6% and generates consistent free cash flow. These are virtues I respect. But virtue in a business does not excuse vice in its price.

My Graham Number — the geometric mean of 22.5× earnings and book value — yields approximately INR 112 per share (EPS ~INR 10.06, BVPS ~INR 55.75). The stock trades at INR 238, a 112% premium to intrinsic value by this measure. At P/E 23.9x and P/B 6.09x, the market has already capitalised every future benefit of Jyothy's brand portfolio into today's price, and then some. Mr. Market is offering this company at a speculative price, not an investor's price. The patient intelligent investor will wait — perhaps for years — until the price descends to offer a genuine margin of safety. Until then, this stock belongs in the "too dear" basket regardless of its business quality.
